newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: African trade groups rule out merger.
newsitem.headline: African trade groups rule out merger.

text.p: The Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) on Sunday ruled out a merger with the Southern African Development Community, with which it has 10 member-states in common.
"The (Comesa) council of ministers has resolved that the two organisations should not merge," the chairman of the council, Malawian Trade Minister Chakakala Chaziya, told Reuters.
"Member states will be free to decide which of the two organisations they would like to belong to. They can also belong to both," Chaziya said.
His remarks followed the announcement on Saturday that Comesa had suspended its secretary-general, Bingu Wa Mutharika, a leading proponent of a merger, for alleged financial irregularities.
Mutharika, who has been suspended for three months, said last week that efforts at merging the two organisations, which often duplicated efforts, would continue.
But Chaziya said: "Our position regarding the two organisations has changed significantly. The council of ministers has agreed that the two organisations continue to coexist."

Two of the states which are members of both trade groups, Mozambique and Lesotho, have said they will withdraw from the 20-member Comesa by the end of the year and remain in the 12-member SADC. They said COMESA was too large to address their concerns.
SADC comprises Mauritius, Angola, Lesotho, Swaziland, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Mozambique, Tanzania, Malawi, South Africa and Botswana.
All these except Botswana and South Africa are also members of COMESA, in addition to Burundi, Comoros, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Madagascar, Rwanda, Sudan, Uganda and Zaire.

Comesa is a common market in name only. It has achieved few of its aims of regional economic integration or intra-regional trade promotion. SADC, with similar goals, is regarded as being better organised and has made far more progress.
Chaziya said a council of ministers meeting, which closed on Saturday, would try to persuade Mozambique and Lesotho against withdrawing from Comesa.
"The council of ministers emphasised the importance of the entire region working in harmony and resolved to hold consultations with Mozambique and Lesotho regarding their withdrawal," he said.
